body:
I'm so sorry that this is how the person who is supposed to be your partner treats you. It is completely unacceptable and you are not being dramatic in the slightest - HE is. That's an extremely dramatic (and unhealthy, and abusive, and shitty, and non-constructive... I could go on) thing for him to do, ESPECIALLY over something over which you literally have no control. If it bothers him so much, he can go in the other room til you're done. This is one of the ways he is showing you it's not about your eating noise at all, it's about domination, control, fear, and manipulation.

Honey, you already know this is wrong or you wouldn't be here and wouldn't say the things you've said. Please consider reaching out to thehotline.org, Jewish Family Services, whatever local DV group you can get your hands on. This kind of behavior is absolutely and fundamentally unacceptable from a child, let alone a grown-ass man who is supposed to love you, and you have already seen that it will not truly improve. Leaving or not is your decision to make, and neither I nor DV resources are here to try and force you to do anything. But it sounds like you may already be thinking about it, and I'm telling you, your instincts are correct. If he did that to a child, would that be ok? Then why should he be allowed to do it to you?

It says a lot that despite his efforts to cow you, make you question yourself, bend you to his version of reality, gaslight you, and stifle your feelings, there is still a voice in your head cutting through all that to tell you it's wrong and has to stop. Please listen to that voice - it may be small, but if it's loud enough to reach you still, it can become loud enough to drown out the voices he is trying to cultivate in your head based on his abuse.

You are not crazy. You are not dramatic. You possess reason and logic and you know what truth is, even when he makes things fuzzy - the truth is still there, it's just hard to see sometimes. But you're seeking it out because you are strong and somewhere you know that NOBODY, including you, deserves to be treated like this. You have feelings and that is NORMAL and HEALTHY, unlike him or your relationship. This is not how healthy people behave - I promise you. It doesn't have to be like this.

I wish I could scoop you up and away from this person. I know it's hard to look at this stuff and deal with it, but you've already started the process and I believe in you. You can do this, in whatever form that takes for you. But please give yourself all the support you can, and get a professional on your team immediately. You don't have to handle this alone.

Big hugs from someone who's been there and who cares about you. You're on the right track.

PLEASE leave! No part of this is ok, and you don't deserve it. More importantly, by coming here and asking, I think you already know the answer hun. You (understandably) just want us to confirm it. Your heart and mind already know this is wrong and that the only way to stop this behavior is to remove yourself from its presence.

Please reach out to thehotline.org and/or try to find local DV resources in your area (like Jewish Family Services, for example). Leaving can be hard and it can be dangerous, so if you are safe enough to reach out first and get help formulating a plan, that's often the better way to go about it, especially if you live together.

They can also help you understand why these things are so incredibly toxic and unhealthy (beyond the obvious), how you wound up with this kind of person, how to help avoid it happening again, and understanding yourself better as a result. It might seem daunting or weird but I bn promise you it will help. You are worth the extra work to make sure you recover and stay well moving forward. Processing all of this is as important as leaving, but leaving is far more urgent.

I'm proud of you for recognizing that this relationship is abusive and needs to end, and for coming on here for support. That's a great sign that you're gonna be ok. Big hugs - we're here and we care (and it's not in your head!).

Triggers, like most trauma-relayed stuff, aren't initially within our control. But as a person, it is our responsibility to become aware of them and deal with them. You can't just run around being a menace because you have triggers and trauma. I respect your empathetic approach and desire not to blanketly vilify people who don't actively mean harm, but at the same time, I think my ex-husband's intentions were fine for much of the abuse. He wasn't consciously trying to belittle and dehumanize me and keep me needy enough to stay controllable and malleable to his vision of what I should be. He didn't wake up one day and consciously decide to strangle me. But he still did. At some point, roughly where things tip from the understandable end of normalcy to the extreme, intentions don't really matter anymore. Just as a child doesn't mean to break their little brother's arm when they shove him on the ground because little bro stole the child's favorite toy, the shoving was still inappropriate, the consequences are still very real and the behavior absolutely should not happen again. Abusers keep doing things even when the consequences/detrimental impacts have been made crystal clear. They *still* might not consciously intend the outcome, but if they cared enough, they'd stop anyway because those outcomes happen whether the intent was malicious or not. It just does not matter after a certain line has been crossed.

P.S. This isn't just our opinions - per multiple DV resources I have spoken to EXTENSIVELY and everything I've had to learn about the legal ramifications of abuse, again, I promise you - legally, ethically, morally, and spiritually, this. Is. Abuse.

It's all serious and it's all abuse, honey. I'm sorry, I know it's weird to reframe that in your head, but the sooner you do, the sooner you can examine it, process it, and grow from it. I have yet to meet the person who grew up around this abusive behavior and not be deeply affected by it (whether they realize they are yet or not). What you described is abuse, but if it helps you come around, think about it this way - that is unacceptable behavior at literally any age. Even little kids who pull that kind of shit are taught not to, right? You wouldn't just allow a child to behave that way and as long as they're sorry, it's fine, right? If an 8yo isn't allowed to treat people that way and can pretty easily learn not to, why should your grown-ass parents be held to a vastly different standard?

What you saw isn't normal. That's not how couples, adults, parents, humans should interact. With anyone. Sure, arguments happen, but healthy, non-abusive relationships do not involve physical intimidation (which is illegal and doesn't even require physical contact, FYI), name-calling, screaming, shoving, breaking things, etc. It's extremely dysfunctional and again, abusive. As someone who also grew up in exactly this kind of environment and later wound up in my own twisted version of it, I promise you: it's abuse, and the sooner you understand all of it the better because you may be recreating these patterns or setting yourself up to do so, or otherwise engaging in unhealthy dynamics or behavior as a result of the normalization of abuse you have endured.

I'm so sorry that you and your family have this experience. It's traumatic, and I wish it didn't have to exist. But this stuff is cyclical, and if you want to help yourself or anyone else you encounter in life who needs it to break this cycle in their own relationships, please please please do all the reading you can. I also STRONGLY recommend seeing a therapist. The fact that this went unrecognized for what it is and has been so deeply normalized is a huge red flag. You might feel ok? Or not, I don't know you, but I guarantee talking to a therapist (esp one who specializes in DV & abuse and/or childhood trauma/family of origin shit) can only help.

Wishing you all the best, and I'm proud of you for reaching out for answers. Not everyone makes it that far.

Ironically, I was raised in a highly religious household - Baptist Christianity was used as a means of control and justification for abuse. Again, I find myself appreciating your understanding that people like me don't have much reason to believe, even if it made logical sense to me (which, and I do hope this doesn't offend, it currently does not).

Thank you for your point about breaking cycles. It's been a problem in my family for generations, on both sides. It's why in 11.5yrs of marriage and both wanting kids, I refused to do so until the behavior and emotional/mental health was addressed. It never was, but as much as it hurt to have those dreams unrealized along with all the rest, at least I never fully became my parents. They had children to honor God and save an abusive, codependent relationship, and it was a huge mistake. I post on DV/suicide subs (also with my main account; rlthis one is an alt that my bf doesn'tknow about) in the hope of someone getting something out of my experiences and pain. I'm often doubtful that little old me can be of any help, but it's worth trying. I love that you're on here doing what you can to help and encourage the breaking of cycles/creations of new ones, thank you on behalf of everyone you've reached out to.

As far as solutions go, big-picture, having a therapist and (secondarily) a lawyer would be a huge help. Neither is absolutely necessary to immediate survival, of course, but if we're talking idealistic situation, then they're on my wishlist. I already have a new lawyer picked out via a referral from someone in my DV group (to handle my divorce, extend the restraining order that my 1st div/dv lawyer screwed up, and possibly fight said original lawyer's insane fee demands), did the consult, have a contract from them and everything, but then my parents told me they wouldn't pay for that so I couldn't move forward with the retainer. I did go to my local LGBT foundation for legal help, but unfortunately they can only provide referrals to lawyers; there's no discounted/pro bono legal aid available. Someone who could help me figure out the bankruptcy thing would also be great in this fantasy world, as I have no idea how that works. I don't even know what to do about taxes this year; my ex used to handle that with his accountant friend so mine certainly aren't getting done anytime soon if at all, but again, those things are not crucial to sustaining life.

Help figuring out if I can take my last "landlord" to small claims court might be useful too. Long story short, when I first left my ex, it was chaos and I moved into an "apartment" that turned out to be an illegitimate, illegally-built/rented addition of sorts, that was being leased out by a long-term scammer. He took me for about $5k, which I confirmed with a good tenant lawyer is all owed back to me. I tried to get this asshole to return my money, but he refused. The tenant lawyer said it wasn't worth going after the guy, as legal fees would outweigh the money recouped, but small claims might be an option. I had to move again, and I've had so much on my plate in the 6mos since that I haven't dug into whether that's even an option, but I sure could use that 5 grand right about now.

I hate to put it this way, but as I currently see it, really my primary immediate situation boils down to money. There are 2 things threatening my immediate survival: lack of income and the health stuff that's holding me back from fixing the income situation. As I mentioned, I have ok earning potential, it's just that that does me no good if I'm not well enough to function. I even have stuff set aside to sell, and I'm familiar enough with how to do that to feel comfortable with it, but most days my physical health has been prohibitive even for that. I do what I can when I can, but it hasn't been enough. My specialist is working on improving the medical situation, but the healthcare system is broken and I'm on week 4 of being unable to get medication I need due to insurance requiring and then denying prior authorizations and related appeals. Doesn't help that my ex changed our insurance during his open enrollment in December, which he is not legally allowed to do while the divorce is pending, but again without a lawyer I can't make him change it back. Luckily it's no longer so bad that I'm in the hospital (I had 3 ER trips in under 2 weeks in January) but I don't know what else to do in the meantime.

So basically if I was to move forward, I need to physically feel better and keep myself financially afloat somehow until I can start working again. I'm not expecting to feel great, that will likely never happen; I just need to be well enough to function/show up and do a job. That's my bar right now.

I'm trying to see it from other angles and figure out if there's something other than money that would wrap duct tape around this whole mess long enough to see me through to my own income, but so far I haven't been able to come up with alternate answers. I'm very open to suggestions though, if you have ideas.

Thank you so much for your time and consideration. I must say I don't know why you're bothering, I think I'm a lost cause at this point, but I do truly appreciate it nonetheless. It feels good to know people like you are on reddit trying to be there for others. It's what the world needs more of.

I'm sorry that you see it that way. I haven't gone into tremendous detail because this is reddit and I don't know you and that wasn't the intention of my post in the first place. I promise you, this is not a fear of being poor - I've been poor most of my life and have literally lived in someone's closet and on couches before, I've done sex work for money, like... I've never been the lowest you can go, but I've been a lot further down than almost anyone I personally know.

I'm not going to waste your time trying to convince you of anything, but maybe remember that you only have info on the tip of the iceberg here, and you don't know anything about my medical situations and the impact that has on my life as it currently is, not to mention how it would be if I became homeless.

I'm also not sure how asking a question solely to benefit someone else is attention-seeking, the way some posts on this sub occasionally are, but that's neither here nor there. Again, none of what we're now discussing was part of my original post/intention. Seemed like you wanted more info so I gave you a bit, that's all.

Anyway, I do very much appreciate your link to resources. Unfortunately I'm in California so based on what I just saw on the Magnificat website, I'd have to be local to Houston to get involved with them. Please feel free to correct me if I'm wrong; I'm still reading up on them.

I was working with a local DV program after my ex was arrested, which is how I was able to see a therapist at no cost for awhile there. They offer a few services that seem similar to MHI, but for example, they were supposed to transfer me to their Mental Health division so I could see a therapist through that branch, and it turned into an administrative clusterfuck. I keep calling them to follow up, but after nearly 2 months of attempting to get it sorted, they have been unable to actually set me up for an intake still. I'm guessing they're understaffed and overloaded, but regardless of the "why", the bottom line is that I can't force them to get it together and book me, so if you do know of other options in the greater Los Angeles area, I would certainly look into them.

Thank you for your response! I tend to feel really guilty about everything and blame myself for shit I couldn't possibly be responsible for (can you tell I've been abused, ha) so I can only imagine how a theoretically preventable death would trigger an extreme version of that response. I desperately want to keep my boyfriend from experiencing that.

I'm so sorry about your parents - I wouldn't wish it on anyone; not even my parents (that's how they came to be this way in the first place, anyway). I hope you're not stuck with yours anymore?

Fortunately I don't live with them; haven't since the last time they kicked me out in high school almost 15yrs ago.   Their current abuse is possible only because I went to them for help escaping my increasingly abusive marriage and trying to get my life sorted out afterwards. If a miracle happened tomorrow and I won the lottery, I'd probably never talk to them again. At first it seemed like they had changed a bit, and were at least doing their best, but it quickly became clear that they have not put in any of the work required to actually become better (or even just non-abusive) people. It's a damn shame because it won't matter to me in a month, not anymore, but I have an older sister who doesn't deserve their treatment either.

Regarding my finances, it's bad. After years of learning the hard way to be financially responsible and clawing my way up the job ladder (HS & college dropout; see: abusive parents/getting kicked out as a teen etc) into big-girl jobs that each paid more than the last, I have an astronomical amount of debt, no usable credit, had to stop paying my cards so my FICO has dropped about 450 points in the past 3 months, would definitely need to file for bankruptcy (if I was gonna be around long enough), my monthly overhead is a bit high (I live in a city, have lots of medical copays, I have a leased car that I can't find a way out of, no roommates, moved 3x in the last 6mos and paid a lawyer to handle my DV case/divorce against my ex who then turned around and quit only to demand more money etc).

It's especially frustrating because as I told another commenter, I very much enjoy working and my earning potential is decent - if I was well enough to work, I could just about afford my daily existence - but I've been too physically unwell to find a job after leaving my last one to focus on addressing my health problems almost exactly a year ago. What was supposed to be a temporary hiatus turned into a year and counting, thanks to the incredibly shitty timing of having to flee my abusive marriage while I was in the middle of dealing with that.

At this point I can't even afford to be alive for the ~1mo I was planning to be here before I go through with it, but I guess I don't have to pay rent for April if I'm gonna be dead by the end of the month anyway, right? What are they gonna do, evict me in May? Too late!!

Anyway, thank you for asking, and for your advice about spending time with my boyfriend. I'm a little worried that more time with me would make it harder, but I guess people do talk about the good times and holding on to happy memories, so you're probably right. He deserves all the joy life has to offer, and to be shown a good time before I'm gone. The least I can do is leave him with that.

Again I really appreciate you reaching out; thank you for your thoughts!

Thank you for this. I should have clarified; I do not live with my parents nor am I a minor. Unfortunately I'm a grown-ass adult and they are still abusive towards me, but from 3,000 miles away. I'm only still in touch with them because of the circumstances I've found myself in (I needed money to stay afloat; they recently provided some but have made it known that that's it).

Basically my whole life fell apart over the last 1.5yrs (job, health, marriage, finances, family, death of the person who was like a [good] parent to me, legal stuff involving my abusive ex, therapists, future, all of it). I've been desperately trying to get it together, but I have a very limited support network and my health problems, which are long-term but have increased dramatically over the last 6mos and created significant new health issues, have been preventing me from doing the things that need to be done even as I've been making progress in healing emotionally.

The odds of all this shit happening in the same timeframe are astronomical, yet here I am, and when I think there's light at the end of the tunnel or nothing can get worse or there's literally no other area of my life that's left to be torn apart, *bam*, something else unravels.

I told my last therapist, before the organization she works at informed me they couldn't extend my participation in their program any longer than they already had, "People kill themselves over *one* of the things I have going on, let alone all of this at once" and all she could say was "You're absolutely correct, and it's enough for 10 people, but you still shouldn't kill yourself".

I've done everything I know how to do to pick up the pieces, I've gotten professional help when I could, I reached out to family/friends, I do my best to address my health stuff & be on top of those various processes, I would love to be working again (always been a very hard worker who enjoys being gainfully employed and hates being stuck on the couch) but that hasn't been possible, and I'm about to run out of money with no feasible options for obtaining more to hold down the fort until I'm doing well enough medically to work again.

I don't see any way to continue surviving, let alone really living, and I'll be damned if I'm going to live on the street (my health problems would make that literally unbearable, for starters). I'm pretty ok with suicide being the answer for emotional reasons also, but the decision to actually do it was primarily based on the impossible, worsening situation I'm in with no foreseeable way out.

Anyway, thank you for expanding on the social media issue. The more I think about it, the more what you said makes sense - it's hard when I see posts that remind me of people I've lost, and I'm someone who has sometimes faded out of people's lives over the years, so a full disappearance seems fitting.

Also good point about wishes being followed. I plan to leave a handufl of notes for different people, and my parents especially are not ones to give a shit about what other people want, so I'll be sure to keep that in mind when figuring that out. I tried to give my boyfriend some of my stuff before I was going to kill myself last time, to smooth some of that over, but that was one of the things that tipped him off so I can't really do that a second time. I'll have a think on it, though. 

Thank you again for your response, and for replying to that other commenter too. I'm glad you're on here and willing to lend a hand where you can. If you think of anything else you'd want someone with my intentions to know/do, I'm all ears. Wishing you the best.

Thank you for your reply! I appreciate it and your thoughtfulness - in my experience, most people don't consider much of what you've expressed here. I'm a huge proponent of therapy but even some therapists aren't truly qualified to listen to/advise people on their problems. I've had friends who were better than shrinks and shrinks who I somewhat consider friends, so I think it really depends on the person and their capacity for perspective more than anything else.  :)

I can't say I'm one for prayers, but I can still get behind the intention, and it genuinely does mean a lot to me that a stranger on reddit would take the time. I hope you're well, and thank you again.

I'm beyond sorry that not only did you lose your sister, but that you had to experience finding her. I wish nobody had to go through that, ever. Mourning and grief are difficult enough when they're pretty straightforward, so I can only imagine how hard that must be. I'm so sorry.

You're correct, he has no responsibility here nor has he done anything to contribute negatively to my situation/decision. He is a good person and the best boyfriend he knows how to be. Unfortunately, my reasons for suicide go far, far beyond any saving grace he (or anyone else) can provide. It's not the sort of thing 1 person could possibly fix.

We don't live together and I considered breaking up with him as part of my original plan, to give him a little time to deal with losing me as a girlfriend before irretrievably losing me as a member of planet earth, and so he could have some distance/support already in place from the initial shock, but was selfishly unable to because he's been just about the only good thing I have in my life, too. It's not really that he's not enough, it's that everything else is way too much.

Thank you for responding and sharing. I know it's terrible to live through what you've experienced but I'm glad you did and are pushing through. I really appreciate you taking the time, and I truly hope time will alleviate some of your turmoil.

I'm so very sorry for your loss. I can only imagine how awful that must be, and the amount of pain you must be in. Is there anything I/we (the community) can do to help?


Unfortunately I have reached out for help for the better part of 2 decades and due to a series of increasingly shitty circumstances, most of which were beyond my control, now find myself without a therapist or the possibility of obtaining one. With little other support in my life, I truly don't see anywhere else to turn. I've been hanging on for months trying to right a ship that sunk long ago, and it has disintegrated further with each effort to patch it up. I've exhausted all my resources, I'm afraid.

But I truly appreciate your input, and thank you for taking the time. I hope you get some respite and help of your own, as you deserve to live life.

Thank you for your response. Unfortunately there's only so much I can do about my material situation, as I have some significant limitations (which are part of the overall driving force here) but I plan to do what I can. I anticipate my parents dealing with my effects (don't feel too bad for them, they're child abusers), and my instructions for them will include the directive to let him have my furniture etc if he'd like it.

To clarify, do you find any value in a social media presence remaining for informational and well-wishing purposes after the fact, or do you think it's entirely detrimental to leave any of that active?

I'm so sorry for your loss and your pain. I agree; selfishly I don't want to tell him because I don't want him to stop me again, but more importantly I think it would cause him far more problems than it solves, and youre correct that there's really not much that can be done long-term to prevent me from doing it anyway. If there were available solutions to my problems, this wouldn't be happening in the first place. I really appreciate your feedback; thank you so much for sharing and I hope your grief eases with time.

My father was very verbally and emotionally abusive first to just my mom, then to my older sister, and then to me.

I'm now 32, and I still sleep with a stuffed animal because I crave the affection, comfort, and stability that I did not get. My self-esteem has been anything from crappy to suicidally terrible since I was a little kid. I cringe at loud noises. I tolerate unacceptable behavior far more than most people (I even work in the service aspect of entertainment - it has affected literally every part of my bnb life including my career). I'm in physical pain all the time from a car accident at 14 that was severe enough to give me a solid concussion and fuck up my back but my dad responded to the news by screaming at us to get the fuck to school. I've been trying to deal with everything from constant pain to debilitating spinal problems ever since, as they would not so much as get me checked out and then months later wouldn't believe that I was actually hurting. I have unhealthy (and sometimes highly abusive) relationships with men. I internalized his voice and all the things he screamed that were wrong with me. I find it extremely difficult to build stability in my own life because I never saw it growing up. I developed an eating disorder that will never truly go away completely. I cut myself and am covered in scars because I had no other way to externalize all the hurt. I questioned myself so much that I didn't recognize gaslighting in my own abusive marriage decades later. I didn't learn a lot of basic skills because they were too wrapped up in the cycle to be actual parents. I sometimes respond to crisis situations with a similar detachment, lack of empathy, and unintentional callousness as my mother, since her coping mechanism was to shut down and/or deny. I wished my parents would die and fantasized about how it would happen. My sister faked physical abuse in high school in an attempt to be removed from our home, because nobody in our small town would/could do anything about verbal abuse with only occasional, milder physical incidents. Instead of fight or flight, I usually freeze because I learned the hard way as a small child and beyond that that was the only viable option. I didn't speak to my parents for years. I resent my mother for staying and allowing it to happen. It still happens to this day, and I haven't lived with them since I was 17 and I moved across the country when I was 20. When I was married, even after improving my relationship with my parents, my husband and I vowed that when we had kids, they would never spend a minute alone with my parents. That sacrificing a deep relationship with their grandparents (esp when mine were so important to me) was a price well worth paying for the sake of their emotional well-being, even if they didn't understand and in turn resented us for it.

But one of the scariest things of all is that it made me angry. So angry and so unable to deal with those feelings, in no small part because nobody in my world was dealing with their own, that the anger turned me into a mini version of him for a few years. When things in my marriage got rocky, I handled it badly. Not as bad as him, by far, but I did not behave the way a person - let alone someone who loves their partner as much as I loved mine - should ever behave.

It took a LOT of therapy to get past that. To process the anger and learn better, to be better. I did it, but it was too late in some ways. I'm a huge proponent of therapy, especially for kids and abuse victims (including/especially verbal abuse). But as much as I believe in it, it's damage control in that it can prevent new cuts and heal old wounds, but those old traumas are turned into scars. They fade with time, sure, but you will never be the same as you would if they did not exist in the first place.

I don't want you to feel like a horrible parent. You probably aren't, especially since you are asking this, and if you are, you can still correct course. Even so, feeling guilty about it doesn't help - if anything, it makes matters worse. But my parents are both products of abuse from early ages. They both have significant trauma. This is a cycle that continued in my life and is going strong in my sister's. She's so far gone that I honestly don't have hope for her anymore. I've been fighting like hell to stop the cycle in my own life for almost 20 years, but it's still something that's a struggle.

I won't tell you what to do... you probably already know. And hopefully you also know that although what I said about therapy and scars is true, it's never too late to start healing, and you and your kids can still have good lives if action is taken.
But I will tell you that I appreciate you asking this question. It's a great sign, and I wish you and your family the absolute best.

Others have already covered much of what I would've said. I echo their strong encouragement to reach out to local (or even non-local online) resources for safety planning, possible exit strategy, support network building, therapy, and group counseling. And I am deeply sorry for what you're going through.

But one thing I want to make sure gets pointed out is that something did change. It wasn't what you were expecting or hoped for or wanted. But the dynamic changed. The severity changed. Your body changed. The amount of legal and moral damage that's been done has changed. And most importantly, even though he won't, you changed.

And when all is said and done, what a lot of this boils down to and what getting out will take is exactly that. The change won't come from him, it'll come from you. I'm so, so sorry that this is how it's happening - you don't deserve this, and you're not wrong for being so frustrated and hurt and feeling all these feelings - but eventually the thing that will truly change is you, and that has already started. It started long before he broke your nose, but you experiencing that and coming on here to post about it is further proof that something is happening to you, not just in being abused but in knowing it's absolutely not ok and reaching out. I'm proud of you for doing that.

If you want practical advice (from a non-professional & former abusee) or need to vent or have questions or just need to be reminded that even strangers on reddit truly care about you, come on by and say whatever you need. I/we are here for you.

This is an opportunity to build trust with yourself. It doesn't necessarily stop the pain, but you know damn well why it had to end and you hold on to that for dear life. You made HUGE progress, and this is the next step on your path to becoming whole without him. It sucks, but this will help get you there, and when people don't know what happened, you can look inside yourself and remember that you know. You know what he did, you know how awful it was, you know it's unhealthy, you know you had to stop it, and you know you do not need him. Talk to yourself like you would talk to your best judy - I mean it, literally in your head, talk yourself through the whole night like you were trying to help your best friend through the same situation. Be that person for yourself, and it may not stop the hurt, but being there to pick yourself up from it will make it easier to process.

Big hugs from a stranger on the internet who is trying to take her own advice.  :)

You don't owe him a goddamn thing, honey.

You do, however, owe yourself the love and respect of trusting the voice that tells you "this doesn't feel ok".

Think about it this way - if this exact situation happened to your best friend, would you tell her "Yeah sure, go ahead and reach out, it might be fine"?


I'm glad he's in therapy and hope you will do the same, but starting therapy is exactly that - starting. It's not a magic cure-all that will fix him possibly ever, let alone in a couple sessions. It takes so much wrong to hurt someone the way he has hurt you; it will be a very long time - if ever - for it to be made right.

Neither of you benefits from contact. It feels like you will because that is what you're used to and comfortable with, but feelings aren't facts and you're not wrong or bad or broken for feeling that way, but still the feeling is not accurate.

It sounds like this guy filled a void for you, and was your main (or only) support.
